question.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.025.$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $p$ | $\,0.900\,$ | $\,0.950\,$ | $\,0.975\,$ | $\,0.990\,$ | $\,0.995\,$ | $\,0.999\,$ | $\,0.9995\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ | $\,3.0902\,$ | $\,3.2905\,$ |

$z=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the table, notice that

$$
P(Z\le 1.96)=0.975.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(Z\ge 1.96)=1-0.975=0.025.
$$

By the symmetry of the standard normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-1.96)=0.025.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14165008/assets/e46e28a748745da14c260af2c39c7c10983b40476c57d8d75a51f0390d2359d2.png)

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.96) & =0.025 \\ P(Z\le -1.96) & =0.025.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required value of $z$ is $-1.96.$
